question: Seoli cell secrets
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Sertoli cells" -> "secrete androgen binding protein" -> "bind testosterone" -> "maintain high testosterone levels in seminiferous tubules" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Sertoli cells" -> "do not secrete testosterone" -> "testosterone produced by Leydig cells" -> 10%
CHAIN: "Sertoli cells" -> "respond to FSH" -> "support spermatogenesis" -> "do not secrete FSH" -> 20%
CHAIN: "Sertoli cells" -> "do not secrete LH" -> "LH acts on Leydig cells" -> "stimulate testosterone production" -> 10%
analysis: Sertoli cells, located in the seminiferous tubules of the testes, are known to secrete androgen-binding protein (ABP). This protein binds to testosterone, concentrating it in the seminiferous tubules and facilitating spermatogenesis. The other options, testosterone, LH, and FSH, are not secreted by Sertoli cells. Testosterone is produced by Leydig cells, while LH and FSH are hormones secreted by the anterior pituitary gland. Therefore, the most likely correct answer is that Sertoli cells secrete androgen-binding protein.
